question:
Select the most appropriate idiom/phrase that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence.

Vennela __made a big fuss about a small problem.__

options.text: Get a taste of your own medicine

solution:
The correct answer is "**A storm in a teacup**".

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** 

__
 
• **"A storm in a teacup" is an idiom that means making a big fuss over a small or unimportant issue**.

 
 
• Example: It is small issue, but you are making a storm in a tea cup. (तूफान बनाना छोटी सी बात पर) 
 
 
 
• In the given sentence, Vennela is exaggerating the importance of a small problem, hence the idiom fits appropriately.
 
• The idiom is derived from the British phrase "tempest in a teapot", which means the same thing.
 
• Other synonyms for this idiom include "much ado about nothing" and "making a mountain out of a molehill".
 
• From the above information, it is clear that the idiom "a storm in a teacup" can substitute the underlined phrase.

Hence, **the correct answer is option 4**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__** 

 
• "**Get a taste of your own medicine**" means experiencing the same unpleasant treatment that one has given to others. (अपने किये का फल भोगना)
 
• "**Barking up the wrong tree**" means pursuing a mistaken or misguided course of action. (गलत दिशा में प्रयास करना)
 
• "**Add insult to injury**" means worsening an already bad situation. (दुःख में दुःख की वृद्धि करना)
